Subject: Partial service blackout during peak window (observed 09:03-09:20 PT)

Hi Lukas / Vanessa,

Quick heads-up — we saw a partial blackout this morning affecting our checkout traffic between 09:03 and 09:20 PT (roughly 17 minutes). Errors were 503 / connection reset and cascaded into a small revenue loss for FastCart during our morning surge.

Can you confirm Redwood's observed availability for our tenant in us-west-2 during that window? We need:
- Exact start/end times you see in platform traces
- Whether the event qualifies for SLA credit under our contract (we're on the Standard hosted plan)
- A log bundle / traces we can attach to our internal incident review

We'd also like an initial estimate of remediation/compensation options so we can brief our finance team. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful — our PM is available 12:30–13:00 PT today.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Ops, FastCart
elena@fastcart.com

Hi team / Elena,

Initial findings from the runtime traces: we observed a control-plane eviction event that caused checkpoint loss for a subset of replicas in the US-WEST-2 cluster. Affected tenant routing showed a sharp increase in request failures starting 09:02:48 PT and a mitigation/route-failover finishing by 09:20:35 PT — total wall-clock ~17m 47s.

What I pulled so far (attached):
- trace_bundle_usw2_20280214.zip (per-req trace fragments, KV cache metadata)
- request_ids_20280214.txt (list of impacted request ids, sample latencies)

Short technical summary:
- Trigger: control-plane eviction during a background firmware update on a subset of accelerators (autoscaler interaction).
- Impact: partial loss of KV cache and repeated tokenization retries for affected shards, producing 503s for traffic routed to those replicas.
- Scope: ~9% of tenant traffic routed to the impacted pool during the window.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Formalize the impact window for entitlement calculation (we have timestamps above).
2) Offer a proportional credit calculation based on impacted minutes and your monthly invoice.
3) Propose a remediation credit + technical mitigations: a one-time 20% discount on next month's Dedicated reservation OR a prorated monetary credit; also recommend pinning your mission-critical routes to a dedicated pool to avoid shared-control-plane maintenance impact.

I'll prepare the raw logs and a short RCA doc for the postmortem. Lukas / David — will need a short blurb on the customer-facing compensation proposal. Elena — are you able to share an estimated invoice amount we should use for the proportional calculation, or would you prefer we provide a percentage-based estimate first?

Attachments referenced above.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com

Subject: Re: Partial service blackout — confirmation and proposed remedy options

Hi Elena — thanks for your patience; summary and proposed next steps below.

Confirmed window (per Redwood telemetry): 2028-02-14T09:02:48 PT to 2028-02-14T09:20:35 PT (17m47s). Vanessa's traces show ~9% of your traffic routed to the impacted pool during that interval.

Entitlement and remedy options we propose (pick one):
- Proportional monetary credit: prorate the impacted minutes against your current monthly invoice. Using the invoice figure you provided by phone (~$84,000/month), the impacted ratio corresponds to an estimated credit of ~$1,090 (final calculation will use exact invoice and minute accounting).
- Service concession: 20% off your next month of Dedicated capacity (applies if you elect to move checkout routing to Dedicated).

We will:
- Produce a final evidence bundle + credit calculation (Doc attached: remedy_agreement_fastcart_20280214.pdf)
- Schedule a 30-minute postmortem with your team to walk the RCA and next steps (proposed slot: 12:30–13:00 PT today; please confirm)
- Add a short action plan to avoid recurrence (recommendation: route-critical checkout traffic to Dedicated pool and bump warmup/keepalive settings)

Next steps for you: please confirm which remedy you prefer (monetary credit or service concession) and whether you want us to proceed with the DocuSign remedy agreement. I've attached the draft and included links to the evidence and the HubSpot deal.

Apologies again for the outage. We'll treat this as a priority and follow through with the postmortem notes.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lukas_meyer@redwood.example.com
